title: In each fixed dimension at least three, every two-coloring of a sufficiently large Cartesian product of cliques contains a product of n-cliques monochromatic in every coordinate direction, with a doubly exponential bound in n^d
author: António Girão, Gal Kronenberg and Alex Scott
difficulty_reason: After ordinary finite Ramsey bounds, elementary sampling estimates and pigeonholing, the remaining proof must construct a recursively consistent product and prove a separate density induction with quantitatively controlled loss in every dimension. The final synchronized coordinate extraction combines these two new constructions to keep the bound doubly exponential for each fixed dimension, exceeding ordinary qualification exercises in Ramsey theory; conservative H1.

proof_review.note: Original Theorem 1.1, only the two-colour case $r=2$ and fixed $d\geq3$, all positive $n$ and the exact original doubly exponential bound; each coordinate direction has its own colour. Full definitions, both Lemmas 2.1 and 2.2 with entire human proofs, and full final closure retained. Ordinary prerequisites: classical finite Ramsey bound $R_r(k)<r^{rk}$, Ramsey (1930), original bibliography [16]; elementary hypergeometric sampling and counting. The proof of Lemma 2.1 chooses $g(d)=(12+2r)^{d-1}$; under selected $r=2$ this is dimension-only. Its last parenthesis literally says $\mathbf v\in B$ although the immediately preceding construction assigns the common $B$ to every $\mathbf v\in U$ and obtains $P\subset U$; all text remains literal. The $d=2$ argument, monotone-array consequence, helper lemmas and parameter choices count zero.
